subject: BuyOps checklist: hosting preference & invoicing route
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: John Ortiz <john.ortiz@acmeretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & buy-ops checklist (hosting + invoicing)

Hi John — thanks for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of procurement questions so we can prepare the right paperwork.

Summary of hosting options we discussed (short):
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest onramp, pay-as-you-go or monthly billing; no infra to run.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity, committed throughput, better unit economics for steady traffic (6/12/24mo commit options).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for regulated data or strict network controls; typically enterprise contract + setup.

Procurement / BuyOps clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Preferred invoicing method: Purchase Order (PO) / Net-30 invoice OR corporate card?
2) Do you require a marketplace purchase (AWS Marketplace/GCP Marketplace) for procurement flow?
3) Any internal vendor onboarding forms (W9, SOC 2 attestation, security questionnaire) we should return to procurement?
4) Desired contract cadence: monthly on-demand vs committed N-month term to capture discounts?

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_1.4.xlsx (pricing matrix), Acme_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (vendor docs we typically return).

Next steps proposed: if PO + marketplace are required we will: (a) confirm whether marketplace listing is acceptable for discounts, (b) prepare a proforma invoice for procurement, (c) provide SOC2 + W9 and standard vendor forms. If card/on-demand is fine we can start with hosted on demand while procurement finishes vendor onboarding.

Available this week to jump on a 20-min buy-ops call to align with your procurement team — what times work?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_1.4.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Acme_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: John Ortiz <john.ortiz@acmeretail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: 2027-05-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & buy-ops checklist (hosting + invoicing)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers from procurement and finance so we can move this along: 

- Invoicing: Procurement prefers PO + Net-30 for anything over $5k/month. Corporate card is rarely used for multi-month commitments.
- Marketplace: We have an internal preference for AWS Marketplace purchases because of our cataloging and central billing. It's not an absolute blocker, but will speed approvals if you have a listing.
- Required docs: W9, bank details for ACH, and a completed vendor onboarding form (attached our standard vendor intake PDF). We also request SOC2 Type II report and an entry-level security questionnaire (we'll send the vendor portal link).
- Commit: Finance is open to a 12-month commit if the pricing is attractive and there's pre-approved SLAs.

Procurement expects to run vendor checks the week of 5/10 and will need a Proforma invoice and vendor contact for onboarding to complete vendor approval. Can you provide a single point of contact for paperwork?

Thanks,
John Ortiz
Director of Platform Procurement
Acme Retail
procurement@acmeretail.com

On Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> (see original message)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: BuyOps checklist: hosting preference & invoicing route — pricing alignment

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding John's procurement responses. Quick notes so we send a clean commercial package: 

What procurement needs:
- W9, bank details, SOC2 Type II — attachable immediately.
- Proforma invoice (PO-ready) showing SKU-level pricing and optional commitment discounts.
- Clarify Marketplace listing status and whether pricing via Marketplace supports the same commit discounts.

Proposal (short):
- Hosted API (on-demand): baseline unit price (no commit). Good for pilot; invoicing monthly via card or direct invoice.
- Dedicated (6/12/24 mo commit): x% discount on per-token and reserved capacity pricing. For Acme, recommend 12mo commit given the traffic profile they described. Include SLA + priority support.
- Private (VPC): enterprise-only; pricing is by quote + setup fees and usually annual invoicing.

Questions for pricing/legal ops:
1) Do marketplace sales support commit discounts or are commits handled off-marketplace (contract + PO) only?
2) Can we offer a limited-time onboarding credit to accelerate procurement signoff (e.g., first month credit if 12mo commit)?
3) Standard lead times: Dedicated provisioning 2-4 weeks after PO; Private 6-8 weeks.

Suggested immediate deliverables: (A) Proforma invoice for PO, (B) SOC2 + W9, (C) short one-pager showing Hosted vs Dedicated TCO for Acme (include expected token volumes). I'll draft the proforma and share a redlined pricing option — please add any constraints.

Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: John Ortiz <john.ortiz@acmeretail.com>, procurement@acmeretail.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-03T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & buy-ops checklist (hosting + invoicing route) — next steps

John — appreciate the quick turn. Action items and attachments below.

What I attached: 
- Proforma_ACME-2027-021.pdf (PO-ready invoice with SKU-level lines for Hosted on-demand and Dedicated 12mo commit pricing).
- Redwood_Pricing_1.4.xlsx (updated with a committed-option column).
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII-report.pdf (redacted summary) and Redwood_W9.pdf.

Notes on marketplace: we are listed on AWS Marketplace for Hosted API but commit discounts are typically not available directly through the marketplace flow. If Acme needs marketplace purchase for accounting, options are: 
A) Short pilot via marketplace (on-demand), then move to an off-marketplace 12mo committed contract for a discounted rate once vendor/PO approvals complete.
B) We can engage marketplace sales to explore a Private Offer (AWS Marketplace private offers can encode commit pricing; will require additional setup and a separate contract).

Next steps I recommend this week: 
- Procurement: confirm whether Acme will accept an off-marketplace PO for a 12mo commit (I attached the proforma to make that easy). If they need a Private Offer via AWS Marketplace, we'll open the marketplace workflow (typically 7-10 business days).
- Redwood: we will standby to submit vendor forms to your portal and provide a single vendor contact (legal-ops@redwood.com).
- Schedule a 20-min alignment with your procurement on Thursday 05/06 or Friday 05/07 to confirm timeline for vendor onboarding.

Would Thursday 05/06 10:00am PT work?

Thanks — attaching files below.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
